title: Five questions to ask any AI marketing vendor, including us
hook: Five questions to ask any AI marketing vendor. Ask us too.
caption:
Five questions to ask any AI marketing vendor. Ask us too.

A demo shows a product on its best day. These questions show the other days.

They cover what the vendor refuses to do, whether the product can explain itself, where it goes wrong, what you keep if you leave, and whose working week has to change.

Send them before the demo and ask for the answers in writing. A written answer gets checked by more people than a spoken one, and you can hold it against the contract later.

The five are in the slides. I would want Galvor held to the same list.

slides.headline: *Five questions* to ask any AI marketing vendor. Including us.
slides.sub: Send them first. Ask for the answers in writing.

slides.headline: What do you *refuse* to do?
slides.body:
Clear limits tell you what a product is for.

A good answer names something the vendor has chosen not to build. 'We do everything' is a warning.

slides.headline: Can it show *why*, in words my team can check?
slides.body:
Ask to see the reasoning behind one recommendation.

If your growth lead cannot argue with it, they cannot trust it either.

slides.headline: What does it *get wrong*, and how would we know?
slides.body:
Every system has blind spots.

A vendor who knows theirs can tell you where a person still has to check the work.

slides.headline: What do we *keep* if we leave?
slides.body:
Your ads taught the system something.

Ask what you can take with you: the tags, the findings, the history. Get it in writing.

slides.headline: Whose *week* changes, and how?
slides.body:
A tool that changes nobody's routine changes nothing.

Ask which meeting, which report and which person will work differently in the first month.

slides.headline: Send these *before* your next demo
slides.sub: Save the list. Ask for written answers.
